simple.meaning: רָמַס (râmaç) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to tread upon (as a potter, in walking or abusively).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 19 times across 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, Isaiah, Ezekiel, and 3 more, beginning at 2 Kings 7:17. Its contexts include family line, death, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָמַס (H7429).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רָמַס (râmaç) / H7429 is traced through 2 Kings 7:17, 2 Kings 7:20, 2 Kings 9:33, 2 Kings 14:9 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to tread upon (as a potter, in walking or abusively)
definitions.usage: oppressor, stamp upon, trample (under feet), tread (down, upon).
definitions.full: H7429. ramas רָמַס verb trample (Late Hebrew id. ; Jewish-Aramaic רְמַס ; compare perhaps Syriac , Arabic , kick (Ba ES 33 Kö ii. 196 ); is bury, and conceal grave ); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular consecutive ׳וְר Micah 5:7 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִרְמֹס Ezek 26:11 ; Psa 7:6 , יִרְמָסֿ Isa 41:25 , suffix וַיִּרְמְסֶנָּה 2Kin 9:33 , etc.; Imperative feminine singular רִמְסִי Nahum 3:14 ; Infinitive construct רְמֹס Isa 1:12 ; Participle רֹמֵס 16:4 ; — trample , of men, with accusative חֲצֵרָ֑י 1:12 , חוּצוֺת Ezek 26:11 (by horses' hoofs), טִיט 41:25 (in simile), compare ׳ר בַחֹמֶר Nahum 3:14 , accusative מִרְעֶה Ezek 34:18 (in figurative); trample down , accusative of person, animal, or thing, 2Kin 7:17 , 20 , so (by horses' hoofs) 9:33 , ׳יִר חַיָּי֫ לָאָרֶץ Psa 7:6 ; 91:13 (|| תִּדְרֹךְ ); subject ׳י Isa 63:13 (figurative; + דָּרַךְ ), subject רֶנֶל 26:6 ; subject beast 2Kin 14:9 (allegory) = 2Chr 25:18 ; Dan 8:7 (vision), of horn, 8:10 ; absolute of lion, ׳וְר וְטָרַף Micah 5:7 (simile); participle as substantive collective tramplers (i.e. devastators) Isa 16:4 . Niph`al be trampled, Imperfect 3feminine plural תֵּרָמַ֑סְנָה בְּרַגֶלַיִם Isa 28:3 (on subject compare Di Du Che Hpt Kö i. 183 ).

occurrences.englishText: The king appointed the captain on whose hand he leaned to be in charge of the gate; and the people trampled over him in the gate, and he died as the man of God had said, who spoke when the king came down to him.
It happened like that to him; for the people trampled over him in the gate, and he died.

You will tread on the lion and cobra.

Let my outcasts dwell with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortionist is brought to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.
The foot shall tread it down,
The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim will be trodden under foot.
“I have raised up one from the north, and he has come,
“I have trodden the wine press alone.
He will tread down all your streets with the hoofs of his horses. He will kill your people with the sword. The pillars of your strength will go down to the ground.

Does it seem a small thing to you to have fed on the good pasture, but you must tread down with your feet the residue of your pasture? And to have drunk of the clear waters, but must you foul the residue with your feet?

I saw him come close to the ram, and he was moved with anger against him, and struck the ram, and broke his two horns. There was no power in the ram to stand before him; but he cast him down to the ground, and trampled on him. There was no one who could deliver the ram out of his hand.
It grew great, even to the army of the sky; and it cast down some of the army and of the stars to the ground, and trampled on them.
The remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples,
Draw water for the siege. Strengthen your fortresses. Go into the clay, and tread the mortar. Make the brick kiln strong.
